title: Spark does not yet control SparkLend — parameters and collateral remain with Sky Core
content:
Three statements in this section establish that SparkLend is documented by Spark but operated by Sky Core.

A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1: "Control of SparkLend is being transitioned to Spark." A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.2.1: parameter modification "is temporarily controlled by Sky Core, but will be transitioned to Spark in the future" — currently exercised by the Core Council Risk Advisor with Phoenix Labs. A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.2.2: collateral onboarding/offboarding likewise, "implemented by the Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor and Phoenix Labs." A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.2 adds that "future iterations of the Artifact will specify operational processes owned by Spark."

The whole section therefore sits under `Management Of Infrastructure Inherited From Sky Core` (A.6.1.1.1.3.2), and inherited turns out to mean documented-but-not-yet-held. Every acting role named — Core Facilitator, Core Council Risk Advisor — belongs to Sky Core, not to Spark. The one Spark-adjacent participant, Phoenix Labs, appears only "in consultation."

This is worth stating explicitly because the Artifact reads, section after section, like Spark's operating manual for SparkLend. It is closer to a register of arrangements Spark is inheriting. The parameter tables are authoritative as a record of state; the process definitions describe someone else's process.

No date, trigger or condition is given for the transition, and no transitional accountability is defined — the Spark Risk Council's scope of review covers proposals under Spark Governance, which these Executive Vote parameter changes are not. During the interval, Spark bears the reputational and economic exposure of SparkLend without holding the controls.
description: Both risk-parameter modification and collateral onboarding are 'temporarily controlled by Sky Core' pending transition, so the Agent's Artifact documents authority it does not hold.
